feature: Asking for a sheet of components: every state shown is one you can see, and the page shares one left edge
summary: Ask now leaves out a state that only deepens one small part a shade (an alert's Pressed darkening its Delete button), only tints its words, adds a ring in nearly the control's own colour, or empties the control into a faint shape (a grey dot as a badge's Empty). A row left with one state is not drawn at all. A title the model sends after the rows now starts on the table's left edge. Each look starts its column with what it paints, so a text button's words sit on the column, not 20 points in. The judges' designed line went from 7 in five of the last six runs to 8 in three of this pass's four.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. A blank picture, then Ask (Command K).

try.do: On a blank picture press Command K and type: create a table of apple like quality base components that show different states and text
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Look across each row: every state changes how the control looks at a glance.
Compare with the sheet before this pass: the alert's Pressed and the badge's grey Empty barely differ from their first look.
Check the title and the row names start on one left edge, and a text button's words start on their column.
Press Command Z once: the whole sheet goes back in one step.

evaluate: Does every state on the sheet look different from the one before it, at a glance?
Would you rather see a weak state than have a row left out (no alert row when its states look alike)?
Do the title, names and every column read as one clean grid now?
Is the empty space right of rows with three states still the first thing you notice?
rough: Ask is still short of the 8-of-10 bar: each of this pass's four runs had one line at 7 (aligned twice, designed twice; 86.4, 80.8, 86, 86.4). Covered by this task (asking-for-a-sheet-of-components-gives-a-clean-t), which stays open.

What holds the 7s now is mostly what the model chooses: wide controls at different widths from row to row, tiny badges, an orange Default alert, variants such as Day/Week/Month shown as states. Covered by this task (asking-for-a-sheet-of-components-gives-a-clean-t).

The skill scored 84 in one run (88.4 before), aligned 7: its model gave Text Field a sixth state and the eval's title check missed. Nothing in it comes from this pass's changes; covered by this task (asking-for-a-sheet-of-components-gives-a-clean-t).

Judges still name the empty right side under rows with fewer states and ask for a row of type styles (which would break the four-size bar). Covered by this task (asking-for-a-sheet-of-components-gives-a-clean-t).
The state chips the editor draws over each copy cover the state names in the window. Covered by the-name-chips-over-component-copies-stay-clear.
No mock covers this surface: it is what Ask makes on the canvas, judged against Apple's design kit pages.
